statement: For an integer v, let occ(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. The function returns a result r and satisfies: if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that nums[i] is even (divisible by 2), then r is even, occ(r) > 0, and for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums) such that nums[j] is even, either occ(nums[j]) < occ(r), or occ(nums[j]) = occ(r) and r <= nums[j]; if no index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) has nums[i] even, then r = -1.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular, it does not fail, panic, or overflow on any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 0 <= r <= 100000.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r != -1, r is even (divisible by 2).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r != -1, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that nums[i] = r.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For an integer v, let occ(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r and r != -1, for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums) such that nums[j] is even, occ(nums[j]) <= occ(r).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For an integer v, let occ(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r and r != -1, for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums) such that nums[j] is even, if occ(nums[j]) = occ(r) then r <= nums[j].
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = -1, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] is odd (not divisible by 2).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For an integer v, let occ(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r and r != -1, for every even integer v with v < r, occ(v) < occ(r).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For an even integer v, let occ(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v, and let occ2(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums2) and nums2[i] = v. Whenever the function returns r on input nums and r2 on input nums2, if occ(v) = occ2(v) for every even integer v, then r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices of 64-bit integers, each with length between 1 and 2000 inclusive, and every element of each slice is between 0 and 100000 inclusive.
